title: प्रथमोनुवाकः
samhita: या त॒ इषुः॑ शि॒वत॑मा शि॒व-म्ब॒भूव॑ ते॒ धनुः॑ । शि॒वा श॑र॒व्या॑ या तव॒ तया॑ नो रुद्र मृडय ॥
krama: या ते॒ । ते इषुः॑ । इषुः॑ शि॒वत॑मा । शि॒वत॑मा शि॒वम् । शि॒व-म्ब॒भूव॑ । ब॒भूव॑ ते॒ । ते धनुः॑ । धनु॒रिति॑ धनुः॑ । शि॒वा श॑र॒व्या॑ । श॒र॒व्या॑ या । या तव॑ । तव॒ तया॑ । तया॑ नः । नः॒ रु॒द्र॒ । रु॒द्र मृ॒डय । मृ॒ड॒येति॑ मृडय ॥

sayana.text:
O Rudra, that arrow of yours which has become most auspicious (shivatama), most peaceful. Similarly, that bow of yours which has become auspicious (shivam), peaceful. And that quiver (sharavya) of yours which is auspicious—with that peaceful arrow, that peaceful bow, and that peaceful quiver, make us (nah) happy (mridaya), give us joy. Their 'peacefulness' consists in the absence of their application against devotees. (2)

sayana.sanskrit:
हे रुद्र ते त्वदीया येयमिषुः शिवतमा शान्ततमा बभूव । तथा ते
त्वदीयं यद्धनुः शिवं शान्तं बभूव । तथा या च तंव शरव्या तवेषुघिस्तया
शान्तयेष्वा तेन च शान्तेन धनुषा तया च शान्तया शरव्यया नोऽस्मा-
न्मृडय सुखय । भक्तेषु प्रवृत्यभावाचेषां शान्तत्वम् ॥ २ ॥


भ०भा०भा० या त इषुः शिवतमेत्यस्याऽऽत्रेय ऋषिः । शंभुर्देवता । अनुष्टु-
प्छन्दः । हे रुद्र या ते तवेपुः शिवतमाऽतिशयेन भक्तानां सुखकरी ।
न केवलं हस्तालंकारमात्रभूता वभूवेति वक्ष्यमाणमनुपज्यते भवतीत्यर्थः ।
"छन्दासि लुहृलङ्कृलितः" इति वतैमाने लिट् । शिवं वभूव ते धनुः । तत्रापि
यच्छब्दोऽध्याहार्यः । यच्च ते धनुः शिवं वभूव ते भक्तान्मति सुखकरं भवति
न केवलं हस्तान्तरमखंकरोति । या च तव शरव्या शिवा भक्तानां सुखकरी
च । गृणातेर्हिंसाकर्मण उभत्यये शरुशब्देनाऽऽयुधमुच्यते । " धुनिः शिमीवा-
ञ्छर्माञ्च ऋजीषी " इति हि इरुयते । ततः समूहे स्वार्थे वा यमत्ययस्तदन्तं
च क्षेपणीये चक्रादौ वर्तते । इरुयते हि "अवष्टष्ठा परापत शरव्ये ब्रह्म-
सखिता " इति । संज्ञाशब्दत्पाञ्चीलिङ्गता । यद्वा पाशादिलक्षणो यमत्ययः ।
छान्दसमन्तस्वरितत्वम् । यद्वा शरवः शरास्तेभ्यो हिता शरव्या इषुधिः ।
पूर्वंवत्स्त्रीलिङ्गता । सर्वासामिषूणां शिवत्वाचदाधारस्य शिवत्वमार्थेना । यथा
ग्रामः मसीदित्विति । यद्वा मा भूविष्णूनामपादानमित्याशास्ते । यथा वक्ष्यते-
" अथो य इषुधिस्तवारे असि्मन्निपेहि तम् " । इति । तया नोऽस्मान्मृडय
सुखय । कयाऽनन्तरमकृतया शरव्यया उपलक्षणत्वाच्चेष्वा तया तेन च
धनुषा । यद्वा लिङ्गसंख्ये अविवक्षिते । व्यत्ययो वा द्वयोः । तैरिष्वादि-
भिरस्मान्मृडयेत्यर्थः । यद्वा करणविभक्तेः ' सुपां सुलुकू ' इति यादेशः ।
एवमीदृशीं शान्तां तनुं गृहीत्वाऽस्मान्मृडयेत्याशास्ते घोरतनूपसंहाराथंम्
' संज्ञापूर्वंको विधिरनित्यः ' इति मृडेलेंघ्रूपधगुणो न क्रियते । ' तवममौ
छन्दसि ' इति तवशब्द् आश्युदात्तः । एतन्मश्रं द्वादशदिनानि चरुभोजीः
जपित्वा कृतपुरश्चरणो विनियोकुं योग्यो भवति । अत्रार्थी ततस्तिलतण्डु-
लयावकामलकल्कमेकादशसहस्सं जुहुयादन्वगनभिजायते । एतेन राजा दुभि-
क्षनिवारणार्थे तिलगुडमिश्रितचरुणा स्वाम्रौ शतसहस्समाहुतीः कारयेत् ।
ततः सुभिक्षमभिजायते राज्ये । ध्यानम्—
" ध्यायेदेवं सुस्मितं स्यन्दनस्थं देव्या साथें तेजसा दीप्यमानम् ।
इष्टिवषासालंकृताभ्यां कराभ्यां शूराकारं स्तूयमानं सुरायैः " ॥२॥
॥ तृतीयास्तृचमाह ॥

bhatta_bhaskara.dhyana: "One should meditate on the God with a beautiful smile, seated on a chariot with the Goddess, shining with brilliance, with his hands adorned with arrows and bow, having the form of a hero, being praised by the best of gods." (2)
bhatta_bhaskara.text:
For 'Ya te ishuh shivatama', the Rishi is Atreya. The Deity is Shambhu. The Metre is Anushtup. O Rudra, that arrow of yours which is 'shivatama'—extremely conducive to the happiness of devotees. It has not merely become an ornament for your hand—this 'has become' (babhuva) is used in the sense of the present tense, as in 'Vedic grammar allows tense shifts'. And your bow which has become auspicious (shivam). Here also, the word 'which' (yat) should be understood. That bow of yours which has become auspicious is conducive to the happiness of your devotees, not just an ornament for your other hand. And that quiver (sharavya) of yours which is auspicious and conducive to the happiness of devotees. The word 'sharu' refers to a weapon, derived from a root meaning injury. It is heard in the Veda: "The roaring one, endowed with powerful deeds, providing shelter, holding the residue of the sacrifice (rijishi)." From that, adding a suffix, the word 'sharavya' refers to things that are thrown, like a discus (chakra) etc. It is heard: "Fly away, O sharavya, with the friendship of Brahman." Because it is a name, it is feminine. Or, it could be formed with a suffix meaning 'beneficial for arrows (shara)', i.e., a quiver (ishudhi). It is feminine as before. Since all the arrows are auspicious, the auspiciousness of their container (the quiver) is implied. Just as one says "May the village be pleased" (meaning the people in it). Or, he prays that it may not be the source of arrows (against us). As will be said later: "Then, that quiver which is yours, place it far away." With that (taya), make us (nah) happy (mridaya). With which? With the quiver mentioned immediately before; and by implication, with the arrow and the bow mentioned earlier. Or, the gender and number are not intended to be specific. With those arrows etc., make us happy—this is the meaning. He prays: "Having taken such a peaceful body, make us happy," for the sake of withdrawing the fierce body.

Having chanted this mantra for twelve days while eating only 'charu' (sacrificial porridge), one becomes fit to use it for specific purposes. If one desires something, he should then offer eleven thousand oblations of a paste of sesame, rice, and gooseberry (amalaka); the desire will be fulfilled. By this, for the removal of famine, a king should have a lakh (100,000) of oblations of charu mixed with sesame and jaggery offered in his fire. Then prosperity arises in the kingdom.

abhinava_shankara.dhyana: Meditation on Lord Maheshvara with resplendent Goddess.
abhinava_shankara.text:
Whatever arrow of Yours, O Rudra, has become most auspicious,
        whatever bow of Yours has become auspicious, and whatever quiver
        of Yours has become auspicious — with that, O Rudra, grant us
        happiness.

Having propitiated the Lord along with all His paraphernalia through the
first mantra, [the devotee] prays for his own happiness through the second:
"ya te ishuh" — "O Rudra, whatever ishuh (arrow) of Yours has become
shiva-tama (most auspicious, most peaceful) — meaning: although it was in
its prior state of a terrible form for the wicked, it has become peaceful in
form through [our] salutation — and whatever dhanuh (bow) of Yours has
become shivam (auspicious in form), and whatever sharavya (quiver) of
Yours has become shiva — sharavya is a particular weapon that serves as an
instrument of harm; [this is known] from the Shruti passage 'avastrina
parapatat —

— sharavye brahma-samshita' (the brahman-sharpened quiver)." Or alternatively,
the word sharavya is derived from the root "shru" with the sense of striking:
sharp arrows (sharuh) are weapons; their collection (sharavar sharavah) is the
quiver; may that quiver be auspicious (shiva). With that sharavya — this is
a synecdoche (upalakshana) — [meaning] with that bow and with that arrow —
mrida nah (grant happiness to us, make us happy). The seer of this mantra is
of the lineage of Atri (Atreya); the meter is Anushtup; the deity is Shambhu.

The dhyana-shloka (verse for meditation) is: "May one meditate upon the
god [Rudra] smiling, standing in a chariot, blazing with radiance together
with the Goddess, with arms adorned with bows and quivers, of heroic form,
praised by crowds of gods."

Perfection (purashcarana-siddhi) is attained by continuous recitation for
twelve days, [performed] at midnight in a way that does not conflict with
one's daily obligatory duties (nitya-karma). This mantra is especially
efficacious for the removal of famine, civil unrest, and similar calamities.

Thus [ends] the second mantra.
